basic_information.short_title: Wao District Hospital Upgrade Act of 2022
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE EXISTING WAO DISTRICT HOSPITAL IN LANAO DEL SUR FROM ITS PRESENT LEVEL 1 WITH A 25-BED CAPACITY INTO LEVEL 1 WITH AN AUTHORIZED 50-BED CAPACITY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Doubles the authorised size of the Wao District Hospital in Lanao del Sur from 25 beds to 50, keeping it at Level I.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The same Organic Law duty behind the region's other hospital acts — comprehensive health service delivery and a general hospital system established by law.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The hospital's authorised capacity doubles. Its buildings, equipment, facilities, operating funds and personnel are upgraded to meet Level I standards at the larger size.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of Wao and surrounding areas in Lanao del Sur
Patients needing admission where beds were short
Hospital staff, whose posts and funding are upgraded
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2022. Delivery depends on the annual Bangsamoro budget.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. Wao District Hospital is authorised to double from 25 beds to 50. It stays a Level I hospital — this is about capacity, not about new specialist services.
in_practice: The hospital remains Level I — the service level does not change
Buildings, equipment, operating funds and personnel are upgraded to match
The hospital integrates the Universal Health Care Act
The Ministry of Health supervises and sets the organisational structure

for_specific_groups.Patients: More beds, but the same level of service — anything needing Level II care is still referred elsewhere.
for_specific_groups.Hospital staff: Personnel are expressly upgraded along with the facility.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2022; construction and staffing depend on annual appropriations.
what_you_can_do: Ask the Ministry of Health about the implementing rules, due within 60 days of enactment
Ask how many of the 50 authorised beds are actually operating
watch_out_for: Unlike most of the June 2022 hospital cluster, this act does not raise the service level — Wao stays Level I.
No peso amount is stated and no completion deadline is set.
Authorised capacity is a ceiling, not a built figure.

key_terms_explained.Level I hospital: A basic facility — emergency care, general medicine, a small ward. Level II adds specialist departments.
key_terms_explained.Authorized bed capacity: The number of beds the hospital may legally operate.
key_terms_explained.UHC Act: Republic Act 11223, the national Universal Health Care law.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhu Al-Qa'dah 16, 1443 / 15 June 2022, approved by the Chief Minister on 12 July 2022.

benefits.headline: Twice the beds at Wao District Hospital.

direct_benefits.how_to_access: Through the hospital, subject to construction

indirect_benefits: Upgraded staff establishment, equipment and operating funds
Universal Health Care provisions integrated into operations
limitations: No change in service level — it remains Level I.

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A patient in Wao who could not be admitted for want of a bed has twice the capacity to draw on once the upgrade is delivered.
A patient needing specialist Level II care is still referred out — this act did not change the hospital's level.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Wao District Hospital Upgrade Act of 2022”.
Section 2 — Policy grounded on Section 22, Article IX of the Organic Law: comprehensive and integrated health service delivery and a general hospital system established by law.

Section 3 — Upgrades the hospital from Level 1 with a 25-bed capacity to Level 1 with an authorised 50-bed capacity, in accordance with national standards of the Bureau of Health Facilities and Services under the Department of Health. The existing building including landscaping, medical and office equipment and other facilities, its operating funds and personnel, are upgraded to include the construction and procurement needed to meet the prescribed standards.
Section 4 — The hospital shall integrate all relevant provisions of Republic Act 11223, the Universal Health Care Act.
Section 5 — The hospital is under the administrative supervision of the Ministry of Health, which determines and approves its organisational structure.

Section 6 — Funding is appropriated from the Bangsamoro General Appropriations for the upgrading, including infrastructure, medical and office equipment, and the annual budget for personnel services, maintenance and operations.
Section 7 — MOH-BARMM shall promulgate implementing rules within 60 days after enactment.
Section 9 — Repeals inconsistent BARMM laws, including those passed under the defunct ARMM, on the operations of the Wao District Hospital.
Section 10 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

citizen_questions.q: Does this make Wao a bigger kind of hospital?
citizen_questions.a: No. It doubles the authorised beds from 25 to 50 but keeps the hospital at Level 1, so the range of services does not change.
The act names no amount — funding comes from the Bangsamoro General Appropriations.

citizen_questions.q: When will the extra beds exist?
citizen_questions.a: The act sets no deadline. Implementing rules were due from the Ministry of Health within 60 days of enactment; construction depends on the annual budget.
